title: Summer ENSO gave uncertain winter sea-level forecast gains beyond local summer level at two Pacific gauges in 1986-2025
abstract: We tested whether July-September Nino 3.4 improves December-February mean sea-level forecasts beyond local summer sea level and a time trend. Separate fits used earlier complete winters only. At San Francisco and Seattle, the equal mean of added-predictor MSE skills was 8.98% for test winters 1986-2025. Its conditional 95% five-year block interval was -32.87% to 32.99%. All six individual site intervals included zero. Removing the 1998 and 2016 test winters reduced Pacific skill to 1.51%. A paired-support check gave 8.79%. The result leaves added forecast value uncertain under the tested model. It does not show that ENSO has no effect. Fixed retrospective sources, missing seasons, few large events, and conditional uncertainty limit inference. This test measures seasonal mean levels, not floods or physical causes. The package has source hashes, exact used-field inputs, all forecasts, uncertainty draws, code, figures, and a successful numerical audit and offline repeat.
